newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends stronger after weekend sell-off.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends stronger after weekend sell-off.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended strongly on Monday after a rumour-inspired sell-off over the weekend.
Rumours had abounded in overseas markets that a New Zealand First Party coalition deal was imminent, bringing about a sharp sell-down to 0.7054 from its US$0.7100/07 Friday close.
"The market got itself a little over-cooked in terms of the rumours that were flying around on Friday night," one Auckland dealer said.
The market had become short and, once again, a lack of supply and high interest rates fuelled a rebound.
Those holding short positions would have to look at stop loss buy orders at 0.7100, he said.
"Domestics are not wanting to be caught short in this currency ... It still costs a lot of money to be short if it goes against you," he said.
The currency finished at US$0.7084/91 and at 67.13, up from 0.7068/75, 66.99 early in the session, having traded a 0.6968-92 range on the day.
Overnight, a range of 0.6975-10 was expected.
As for the rumour mill, the dealer said: "I still don't think it's a good idea to sell kiwi until we get something factual."
